aggregate_initial_judgment: Read before opening seat totals. Claim: AIDA collects demonstrations by letting a privileged rule teacher act through the student's deployed skill interface (search/turn/nav_to_point/pick/place), adds templated spatial-reasoning labels and a train=deploy prompt/history/output harness, and SFTs Qwen3-VL-8B (LoRA). Key evidence: Table 2 is a controlled teacher comparison (same model, interface, annotation, harness; equal 28,480-example AIDA sets vs 152,478 relabeled OWMM examples; three evaluations, one training seed); Table 3 a cumulative harness stack; Table 1 headline 71.76% vs baseline numbers copied from OWMM-Agent (different base models, and the copied rows' percentages imply ~306 episodes vs 170 here); EB zero-shot transfer of the OWMM policy 0.02->0.55 on an unseen simulator; real robot 38% without a trial count. Teacher privilege is explicit and excluded from student prompts. Expected: component_training, transfer via the counted cross-simulator run, scoped support, strong E.causality for the teacher claim only.

paper.title: Look Before You Move: Agent-Interface-Aligned Supervision for Open-World Mobile Manipulation
paper.central_claim: Agent-interface-aligned privileged-teacher demonstrations, active target acquisition, spatial reasoning labels and a shared harness teach a VLM mobile manipulation: 71.76% on 170 held-out OWMM episodes, 38% real-robot success without additional training, and applicability to EmbodiedBench navigation.
paper.scope_note: In scope as student training from a harness teacher: the teacher is a privileged rule policy acting in the student's skill harness (not a frontier-LLM harness); the student VLM pilots the same harness. K505 records this case.
